Ok so people always ask me how sourdough actually works and the honest answer is i didnt really get it for like a year of baking it. Here's the version i wish someone had told me.

You're not adding yeast. The yeast is already there — its floating in the air, its on the flour, its on your hands. When you mix flour and water and just leave it out, you're basically building a little apartment for the wild yeast and bacteria to move into. Feed them every day (thats the "discard and refeed" thing everyone complains about) and they wake up and get hungry.

The bubbles? thats them eating the sugars in the flour and burping out gas. The sour taste is from the bacteria, not the yeast, theyre a team. Warmer kitchen = faster everything, colder = slower. Thats genuinely most of it.

The part nobody tells you is that its mostly about patience and reading the dough instead of the clock. My first ten loaves were frisbees. Number eleven was edible. Now i can do it half asleep. So if yours sucks right now, congrats, thats the normal part, keep going.
